{"input": {"clarifying_context": "Customers: Internal ML engineering teams, enterprise customers using the AI training platform (e.g., Ledger AI division, BioTech Labs data science group, RoboDrive ML team)
Business justification: Lack of experiment tracking is slowing down iteration cycles and making it difficult for enterprise customers to meet auditability and governance requirements. At least 4 enterprise accounts have flagged experiment observability as a gap during renewal discussions, representing ~$4.2M in ARR. Strategic investment in ML platform maturity and competitive parity with platforms that offer built-in tracking.
User problem: Users cannot compare experiment runs across training strategies (LoRA, SFT, OSFT), track how hyperparameter changes impact model performance, or inspect metrics and artifacts in a centralized location. Debugging, optimization, and reproducibility are manual and fragmented — teams resort to ad-hoc spreadsheets and custom scripts to track experiments, leading to lost context and unreproducible results.
Scope: Single focused enhancement — adding MLflow integration as a cross-cutting concern across the existing pipeline. No structural changes to training modularity or Eval Hub integration. Touches validate_dataset (dataset metadata logging), training components (metric emission), evaluate_with_eval_hub (forwarding evaluation outputs), and register_model (attaching run IDs). One new component: log_to_mlflow.
Success criteria: End-to-end pipeline runs successfully with MLflow logging enabled. Each run logs parameters (strategy, hyperparameters, dataset version), metrics (training loss/accuracy, Eval Hub results), artifacts (model artifacts, logs, evaluation reports), and lineage (pipeline run ID, model version, dataset reference). MLflow run is linked to pipeline run, Model Registry entry, and Eval Hub evaluation results. Users can compare runs in MLflow UI, inspect metrics and artifacts, and trace experiment lineage without external tooling.", "priority": "Undefined", "prompt": "Our AI training pipeline supports multiple training strategies like LoRA, SFT, and OSFT, and we already have Eval Hub integration for evaluation, but we have no centralized experiment tracking. **Was skipping revision the correct decision?**

3. **Review quality is thorough**: The review provides detailed, actionable feedback on what would improve the WHY score. The feasibility review is comprehensive, identifying real architectural considerations (MLflow integration points, authentication, Eval Hub linkage, multi-tenancy). Strategy considerations are flagged appropriately.

The RFE is already high quality (9/10), and the only gap (WHY = 1/2) requires real customer data that an automated pipeline cannot and should not fabricate.
